title: Your appeal, my son-in-law
odia:
ତୁ ଗୁହାରି କରୁଚୁ ଯାହାକୁ
ମୁଁ ଜୁଆଇଁ କରିଚି ତାହାକୁ।
literal_meaning: The person you are appealing to—I have made him my son-in-law.
meaning_odia: ତୁମେ ଯାହାଙ୍କୁ ଗୁହାରି କରୁଛ, ସେ ମୋର ଜୁଆଇଁ—ଏହା କହି ବକ୍ତା ନିଜର ପାରିବାରିକ ସମ୍ପର୍କ ଦେଖାଉଛନ୍ତି। ଆମ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟାରେ, ଏହା ନିଜ ପ୍ରଭାବର ଦାବି ଏବଂ ଗୁହାରି ଶୁଣୁଥିବା ବ୍ୟକ୍ତିଙ୍କ ନିରପେକ୍ଷତାକୁ ନେଇ ସନ୍ଦେହର ଇଙ୍ଗିତ। ଗୁହାରିର ଫଳ କିନ୍ତୁ ଧାଡ଼ିରେ କୁହାଯାଇନାହିଁ।
explanation: The reply turns the other person’s hoped-for recourse into a claim of personal influence: the person hearing the appeal is the speaker’s son-in-law. Read editorially, the boast raises a question about impartiality. The saying supplies the relationship and the challenge, while leaving the outcome of the appeal unstated.
usage_example: Original imagined example: During a disagreement, one person says they will ask a mutual acquaintance to intervene. The other boasts of a close family tie to that acquaintance, echoing this saying.
cultural_context: The paired words ଯାହାକୁ and ତାହାକୁ point to the same person from two directions: someone receiving a plea and someone connected to the speaker by marriage. That shift supplies the force of the reply.

odia_summary: ଗୁହାରି ଶୁଣୁଥିବା ବ୍ୟକ୍ତିଙ୍କ ସହ ନିଜ ପାରିବାରିକ ସମ୍ପର୍କ ଦେଖାଇ ପ୍ରଭାବର ଦାବି।
english_summary: A family connection is invoked to challenge another person’s appeal.
